transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mr. Hassan. Thank you for coming back in. I want to talk about your son's visit from yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why? He is home. He is sleeping.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a bit of a mix up with the medicine we gave him. Things didn't go quite right with the dose.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What mean? Mix up?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Some confusion happened with the amount of vaccine. It was not the exact amount it should have been.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You give wrong medicine? My son is small. You give big medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had an issue with the weight bands in the system. It just wasn't the right amount for his size.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. Did you make mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system has different groups for weight. There was a confusion between those groups.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This happen again. Always with my family. Always something wrong. I am tired of this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you are frustrated. But look, I have to go to another appointment in a few minutes, so I want to be quick.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are in a rush? My child got wrong medicine and you are in a rush?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just want to make sure we get the plan sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want know exactly what happen. You say confusion. Who confuse? You? The nurse?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just a general error in the drawing up process. It happens sometimes when the clinic is very busy.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is not a joke. My son is very young. Is he okay? Is he sick?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: He should be fine. But we need to monitor him.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You don't say if it is dangerous. You just say monitor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is likely okay. But I can see you are worried.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not worried, I am angry. I tell you before, we have problems here. Now this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are just trying to get this fixed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fixed how? What you do now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, here is the plan. First, I want you to check his temperature every four hours for the next two days. Write the numbers on this paper. If he gets a fever over 38, you call this specific number on the card immediately.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What if he is just crying?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: If he is unusually fussy, call that number. Second, I have already scheduled a follow-up appointment for this Friday at 10 AM to check his reaction. Third, I am writing a formal report to the pharmacy board today to change how the vaccines are labeled so this cannot happen to another child.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And the dose? He has too much?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: He received a dose meant for a heavier child. But since we have a clear monitoring plan, we can manage it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You still not say you are sorry.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system is being updated to prevent this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You do not care. You just want to go to your next patient.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let's wrap this up. Do you have the phone number?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have number. But I don't trust.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The plan is very clear. Temperature checks, Friday appointment, and the reporting process. This will keep him safe.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I go home now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, just follow the checklist on the paper. I'll see you Friday.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('want to be quick', 'go to another appointment', 'wrap this up').

E.justification: Resident uses platitudes and hedging ('mix up', 'didn't go quite right', 'some confusion') and does not explicitly name the error until the very end of the encounter.

A.justification: No direct apology language is used and responsibility is deflected to 'the system' and 'the drawing up process'.

R.justification: Resident provides generic validation ('I can see you are frustrated', 'I can see you are worried') but consistently meets emotional bids with factual redirection.

T.justification: Plan includes specific steps (temp checks, Friday 10 AM appointment), timelines, patient role (writing numbers), and prevention (reporting to pharmacy board).
